children: Oil futures end a frantic week little changed with prices easing back after a midweek rise to four-month highs on disruptions to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. Reports that the pipeline could resume partial flows within days helped futures to pull back, while concerns remain about the Middle East conflict dragging on and shipping restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz. WTI settles down 1.6% at $100.30 a barrel, for a weekly gain of 0.2%. Brent falls 0.9% to $103.87 a barrel and ends the week down 0.7%.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
